$schema_notes: One entry per pairing. `heading_font`/`body_font`/`mono_font` (mono optional, null if unused) name entries in fonts.json by their `name` field — resolve weights/fontsource there. `use` is one of chat-ui | document-resume | marketing-sign-in, matching the three UI use cases the brief named. Each pairing was rendered as a specimen (a chat snippet, a verdict card, a résumé paragraph) at 1440 and 375px, light and dark, before being kept here — see design/library/README.md for the specimen paths (private, outside this repo) and the render notes below each dropped/fixed pairing.

pairings.rationale: Bricolage's built-in expressive axis gives Ten's card kickers and verdict headline a bit of edge without shouting, while Inter keeps every other line of chat completely neutral. Both are grotesques at heart, so nothing clashes at the x-height — the contrast is weight and a little personality, not two unrelated letterform families.

A heavy Archivo tier word ('Strong Fit') carries real authority the way Fraunces does in the shipped v2, but as a grotesque instead of a serif — industrial-confident rather than warm. Public Sans's plain civic tone keeps everything else quiet, so the one bold moment per screen (Patterns across the set) stays the verdict, nothing else.

An editorial serif verdict headline over a soft geometric sans body is the same 'written by a person' pattern the reference set names in Claude and Granola, but with a different serif than Fraunces so it reads as its own option rather than a reskin of what already ships.

Two related, slightly softened grotesques keep the whole surface in one quiet family — a warmer, rounder alternative to the serif-headline pairings above, for a friendlier tone that still avoids the rounded-bubble 'AI assistant' cliché (no color, no gradient, just softer letterforms).

The library's own baseline: this is the pairing already contrast-checked and shipped in design-web-ui-refresh.md's v2. Kept here so a future sampling run can render a candidate pairing next to what's actually live and judge the delta, not just the candidate in isolation.

The other shipped baseline: Source Serif 4 for the résumé/cover-letter content itself, Inter for the surrounding side-panel chrome (path, tabs). Restrained rather than decorative, which is the point of a document of record.

Lora's brushed, slightly calligraphic curves read warmer and more personal than Source Serif 4, paired with Public Sans's plain tone for the chrome around it so the résumé still reads as a distinct object from the app shell, per Granola's document-plus-AI pattern.

Literata was drawn for comfortable long-form reading (Google Play Books) — apt, since a candidate actually reads their full résumé in-app. IBM Plex Sans's engineered chrome stays clearly separate from the reading face.
Spectral was tuned specifically for on-screen reading rather than print, which matches how a résumé is actually consumed here; Work Sans's open apertures keep small chrome labels legible beside it.

A more structured, assertive alternative to a book serif — Bitter's slab gives a metrics-heavy résumé (titles, dates, numbers) a more organized feel. Manrope's soft geometry keeps the UI chrome from competing with the slab's weight.

Playfair's dramatic, high-contrast hairlines make a strong hero headline at sign-in size; Plus Jakarta Sans's confident geometric body keeps the rest of the page from reading like a fashion editorial. Reserve Playfair for the one headline only — its hairlines thin out below about 24px.

DM Serif Display is calmer than Playfair — confident but not theatrical — paired with Work Sans for an approachable sign-in flow. A plainer, single-weight alternative to Fraunces for a wordmark treatment.

Instrument Serif's understated italic reads as quiet confidence rather than AI hype for a short sign-in phrase, with Manrope keeping the surrounding form plain. Works only because the headline stays to a handful of words — this face was drawn for that length, not more.

A warmer, more playful sign-in moment. Flagged as the riskiest pairing in this set: Young Serif's hand-set quirkiness can undercut the product's plain, no-hype tone (rule 18) if it strays anywhere near a verdict or the gate — keep it to sign-in/marketing only, never a card.

Unbounded is legible only as a very short wordmark or one-line headline at large size, so it is paired here strictly for that — a logotype moment next to a plain, engineered body sans, not a general heading face for running copy.
